newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Schering-Plough sees brisk Asia growth.
newsitem.headline: Schering-Plough sees brisk Asia growth.

text.p: U.S. pharmaceutical company Schering-Plough Corp expects brisk growth in Asia Pacific and to double market share in some countries in the region in the next three years, a senior official said on Friday.

"We have been growing (in Asia) at 20-22 percent in the last two years. We expect to grow 25-30 percent a year for the next three years," Schering-Plough's executive vice president Raul Cesan told a news conference.
Schering-Plough's sales in Asia, which it defines as including Australia and South Africa but not Japan, was US$260 million in 1996, officials said.
Cesan said the company was investing heavily in both manufacturing facilities and marketing in the region.

He said it had invested about US$250 million in six finishing plants in the region, a chemical plant in China and its new Singapore $300 million chemical plant in Singapore, which was officially opened on Friday.

"Schering-Plough has been growing so fast that this (Singapore) plant is coming on not a minute too soon. We are running out of capacity and this will become our primary centre of production," Cesan said.
He said the company's growth in the region was faster than the average sales of Schering-Plough as a whole.
Schering-Plough recorded global sales of US$5.7 billion in 1996, an increase of 11 percent over 1995.
"Yesterday I approved a couple of investment programmes of marketing operations to double our market share in some of these markets in the next three to five years," Cesan said.
These countries included South Korea and the Philippines, where its market share was just 0.65 percent and 1.97 percent respectively, said Ian Price, vice president for the Far East and South Africa.
Price said the Asian pharmaceuticals market, excluding Japan and China, was valued at about US$15 billion, with Schering-Plough's share at about 1.5 percent.
The market in Asia was growing at about 10 percent annually, Cesan said.

The Singapore plant will produce about 100 tonnes of ingredients for products like non-sedating antihistamine, prostate cancer treatment, cardiovascular therapy, asthma treatment and steroid compounds for dermatogiocal use.
Exports to the company's finishing plants worldwide were expected to start from the third to four quarter this year, said Patrick Yeung,the company's managing director in Singapore.
Schering-Plough also signed an agreement on Friday to licence and test analytical software products from the National University of Singapore's BioInformatics Centre.
